stories.headline: Israel certifies its election result, rejecting fraud claims
body: Israel's election committee certified last week's results, finding no evidence of fraud.
Netanyahu's bloc won 53 seats and Eisenkot's 48; Arab-led parties won a record 19.
No bloc has the 61 seats needed, and President Herzog begins talks.
stories.vc: A long coalition fight delays Israel's budget and policy decisions.

stories.headline: Death toll from Russian strike on Ukraine aid centre rises to 40
body: Ukraine says 40 people died in Monday's Russian strike on an aid centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia.
More than 30 people may still be under the rubble.
Kyiv is due at US-brokered ceasefire talks next week.
stories.vc: Ceasefire talks next week matter for Ukraine's rebuilding costs and energy markets.

stories.headline: Yemen's government forces push further into Houthi-held mountains
body: Yemen's government forces say they pushed deeper into the al-Dahida mountains in al-Jawf province.
They say jets and drones backed the advance against the Houthis.
Fighting is also rising in al-Dhalea, Lahij and Taiz.
stories.vc: Fighting in Yemen keeps Red Sea shipping risk and insurance costs high.

stories.headline: Bengaluru's Pink Line to open on 13 November
body: PM Modi will open the elevated section of Bengaluru's Pink Line on 13 November.
It will take the city's working metro network past 100 km.
The state aims to grow the network to 170 km.
stories.joke: Finally, a line in Bengaluru that moves.
stories.vc: More metro reach raises property values near stations and cuts commute costs.

stories.headline: Nykaa's profit triples to ₹101 crore
body: Nykaa's quarterly profit rose 207% to ₹101.2 crore as revenue grew 28% to ₹3,006 crore.
Beauty became more profitable and fashion losses narrowed.
It will also buy 82% of makeup brand Simply Nam for up to ₹33 crore.
stories.joke: Glow-up, but for the balance sheet.
stories.vc: Profitable listed consumer tech gives investors confidence in India's next IPO wave.

stories.headline: PhysicsWallah returns to profit with ₹143.6 crore
body: PhysicsWallah made a ₹143.6 crore profit last quarter, up from ₹69.7 crore a year ago.
It had lost ₹88.3 crore in the previous quarter.
Revenue rose 18% to ₹1,242 crore.
stories.joke: Physics says what goes down must come up. Sometimes.
stories.vc: An edtech back in profit helps a sector that lost investor trust after the boom years.

stories.headline: NPCI sets up a new arm for AI and blockchain
body: NPCI, which runs UPI, has set up NPCI Tech Solutions to work beyond payments.
It will focus on AI, blockchain and digital financial infrastructure.
Vishal Kanvaty will lead it as MD and CEO.
stories.joke: UPI's parent wants a side hustle too.
stories.vc: NPCI moving into new tech areas could compete with or partner fintech startups.

stories.statLabel: toughest seats with women Democratic nominees
stories.headline: Women candidates helped Democrats flip the US House
body: More than half of competitive House races this year had women candidates.
Women were Democratic nominees in 20 of the 41 toughest Republican-held seats.
Democrats have flipped 31 House seats so far.
stories.vc: Women candidates' strong showing will shape which donors and groups get more funding next cycle.

stories.headline: Gina Hinojosa becomes Texas' first Latina governor
body: Gina Hinojosa defeated Governor Greg Abbott, who was seeking a fourth term.
She will be the first Latina to lead Texas.
She campaigned on corruption, prices, schools and data centres.
stories.vc: Her focus on data centres could change how Texas courts big tech projects.

stories.headline: Amy Acton becomes Ohio's first elected woman governor
body: Doctor Amy Acton beat Vivek Ramaswamy by nearly 8 points to win Ohio's governor race.
She is the first woman elected governor in Ohio.
Ohio had not elected a Democratic governor in 20 years.
stories.vc: A public-health doctor as governor may push health spending up the state agenda.
